# ARTIFICER.ASIA — Full Description

> Hardware access and deployment network connecting hardware providers with qualified hackathons, universities, and builder communities across Asia.

Canonical site: https://artificer.asia · Ref: AA·2026 · Field Manual Ed. 01

## What ARTIFICER.ASIA is

ARTIFICER.ASIA is a hardware access and deployment network connecting hardware companies with qualified hackathons, universities, and builder communities across Asia. We give qualified programs access to professional hardware at no cost, while giving manufacturers a repeatable way to put their equipment into builders' hands, support its use, recover it, and document what was created.

## The two sides

- Side A — Organizers: qualified hackathons, universities, student technology programs, and builder communities can request professional hardware at no cost, subject to program review and equipment availability.
- Side B — Providers: hardware manufacturers and technology companies retain ownership of their equipment. ARTIFICER.ASIA takes temporary custody for approved deployments, matches hardware with qualified hackathons and university programs, coordinates setup and participant access, provides technical enablement where needed, recovers and reconciles equipment afterward, completes a documented return handoff, and documents what builders created.

## Who can request hardware

- Hackathons
- Universities
- Student technology programs
- Research or maker communities
- Nonprofit technical programs
- Other structured builder events in Asia

## Who can provide hardware

Hardware manufacturers, semiconductor companies, robotics companies, IoT companies, developer-hardware companies, DevRel teams, ecosystem teams, partnerships teams, developer-marketing teams, and technology partners that want qualified builders to use their hardware.

## Hardware categories

Categories describe the kinds of professional equipment ARTIFICER.ASIA can coordinate for selected programs. Availability of any specific device is confirmed during review — no device listed here is guaranteed for a given event.

- Robotics and autonomous systems — robots, actuators, and autonomous platforms for movement and control projects.
- AI and edge-computing devices — accelerators and edge systems for on-device AI and inference work.
- Sensors and IoT equipment — environmental, motion, and connectivity sensors for networked builds.
- Cameras and imaging systems — visible, depth, and machine-vision imaging for computer vision projects.
- Drones and aerial technology — aerial platforms for mapping, sensing, and flight-focused builds.
- Smart glasses and spatial-computing devices — wearable and spatial interfaces for augmented and mixed-reality experiments.
- Microcontrollers and prototyping systems — boards, kits, and bench tools for rapid electronics prototyping.
- Other specialized technical equipment — category requests reviewed case by case against event needs.

## Program review criteria

Selection considers technical readiness, event organization, participant capability, equipment suitability, and the likelihood of meaningful use. Requests are reviewed for event suitability, technical readiness, and equipment availability. Programs and equipment are subject to review and availability.

## Organizer workflow — request to return, in six steps

1. The organizer submits an equipment request.
2. ARTIFICER.ASIA reviews the event and technical requirements.
3. Suitable equipment is identified and matched with the program.
4. Hardware is delivered and prepared, with onsite support provided where needed.
5. Equipment use and resulting projects are documented.
6. Devices are reconciled, packed, and returned to the hardware provider.

## Provider deployment model — from offer to documented return

- Program Matching — identify programs suited to the provider's hardware, target builders, technical requirements, geography, and developer goals.
- Deployment Preparation — coordinate receipt, inventory, technical preparation, setup, and participant access before each approved deployment.
- Onsite Stewardship — when needed, provide onsite stewardship for participant access, basic technical enablement, troubleshooting, and equipment recovery.
- Outcome Documentation — providers receive a deployment record showing where the equipment went, who used it, how it was used, what was built, technical feedback, available media, and potential future deployment opportunities.

## Custody model

Hardware providers retain ownership throughout the deployment. ARTIFICER.ASIA takes temporary custody shortly before an approved program, manages deployment and recovery, and ends custody with a documented return handoff. Unless separately arranged, between-event storage, warranties, and substantive repairs remain with the hardware provider.

## Repeat deployment

A successful activation should make the next one easier. ARTIFICER.ASIA documents equipment setup, support requirements, builder use cases, technical feedback, and outcomes so proven hardware and program formats can be carried into future deployments across Asia. Hardware returns to the provider between programs unless another custody arrangement is agreed.

## Outcome documentation

Deployment records may include: equipment model and serial number; event, country, and venue; participating teams and builders; equipment utilization; prototypes and demonstrations; code repositories where available; technical feedback; photos and video where consent is provided; and potential future deployment opportunities.

## Geographic focus

ARTIFICER.ASIA focuses on hackathons, universities, and builder communities across Asia, subject to program feasibility and equipment availability.

## Current pilot — CoCo City Goa

Initiative 001. Next deployment: the CoCo City hackathon in Goa, 17 October 2026, 09:00 IST, in conjunction with Invisible Garden and Common Compute. The pilot will establish a repeatable system for selecting equipment, coordinating delivery, preparing devices, supporting builders, documenting projects, and recovering and returning equipment.

Roadmap: CoCo City pilot → additional Asian hackathons → university programs → regional hardware-access network.

Equipment is also intended to support future hackathons and university programs, including prospective initiatives connected with Chiang Mai University and IIT Bombay. These institutions are not confirmed partners.

## Important limitations

- Access is provided to approved programs at no cost, subject to program review and equipment availability.
- Specific equipment availability is confirmed per program.
- ARTIFICER.ASIA does not operate as a public hardware rental storefront. No rentals, no storefront.
- For temporary deployments, hardware providers retain ownership and equipment is returned after the approved deployment unless another custody or ownership arrangement has been agreed.
